issue_context.title: Null cases not handled properly for some list operations
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
test = pl.DataFrame({"a": [["hi"], [], None]})
print(test.select(pl.col("a").list.contains("hi")))

test = pl.DataFrame({"a": [["hi"], [], None]})
print(test.select(pl.col("a").list.len()))
```


### Log output

```shell
shape: (3, 1)
┌───────┐
│ a     │
│ ---   │
│ bool  │
╞═══════╡
│ true  │
│ false │
│ false │
└───────┘
shape: (3, 1)
┌─────┐
│ a   │
│ --- │
│ u32 │
╞═════╡
│ 1   │
│ 0   │
│ 0   │
└─────┘
```


### Issue description

Some list operations that return a non list type (e.g. `contains` and `len`) result in (arguably) incorrect values for null values. In the example above, `contains` returns `False` and `len` returns `0`

### Expected behavior

operations on null values should just return null

review_comments:
This should happen in the `is_in` implementation
Can you confirm the expected behavior for `is_in` null propagation? It appears that `is_in` does not currently propagate nulls at all:

```python
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "a": [1, 2, None, 3, None, None],
        "b": [[1], [1], [1], None, None, [None]],
    }
)

df.with_columns(
    pl.col("a").is_in("b").alias("a_in_b"),
)

# ┌──────┬───────────┬────────┐
# │ a    ┆ b         ┆ a_in_b │
# │ ---  ┆ ---       ┆ ---    │
# │ i64  ┆ list[i64] ┆ bool   │
# ╞══════╪═══════════╪════════╡
# │ 1    ┆ [1]       ┆ true   │
# │ 2    ┆ [1]       ┆ false  │
# │ null ┆ [1]       ┆ false  │ <- LHS is null
# │ 3    ┆ null      ┆ false  │ <- RHS is null
# │ null ┆ null      ┆ false  │ <- both sides are null
# │ null ┆ [null]    ┆ true   │ <- LHS is null, RHS contains null
# └──────┴───────────┴────────┘
```

Is that expected behavior? 

On further thought, I'm going to close this as the behavior of `is_in` null handling has been discussed before. It probably makes sense to wait for a decision on one/all of these:

https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/18730
https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/18728
https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/12591

As they share an implementation, `list.contains` currently operates the same as `is_in`:

```python

df.with_columns(
    pl.col("a").is_in("b").alias("a is_in b"),
    pl.col("a").is_in("b").alias("b contains a"),
)

# ┌──────┬───────────┬───────────┬──────────────┐
# │ a    ┆ b         ┆ a is_in b ┆ b contains a │
# │ ---  ┆ ---       ┆ ---       ┆ ---          │
# │ i64  ┆ list[i64] ┆ bool      ┆ bool         │
# ╞══════╪═══════════╪═══════════╪══════════════╡
# │ 1    ┆ [1]       ┆ true      ┆ true         │
# │ 2    ┆ [1]       ┆ false     ┆ false        │
# │ null ┆ [1]       ┆ false     ┆ false        │
# │ 3    ┆ null      ┆ false     ┆ false        │
# │ null ┆ null      ┆ false     ┆ false        │
# │ null ┆ [null]    ┆ true      ┆ true         │
# └──────┴───────────┴───────────┴──────────────┘
```
